title: Budoids - mESC-derived 3D organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells
mechanism: Mouse embryonic stem cells are driven by a 7-day small-molecule protocol into heterogeneous 2D cultures containing cells with limb-bud mesoderm, surface ectoderm and AER properties; dissociating and reaggregating them in low-attachment plates forms free-floating organoids ('budoids') with limb-bud-like features that undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days. The AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities and enhance tissue polarisation permitting distant cartilage formation - that is, the signalling centre's role in cell fate AND spatial organisation can be dissected without an embryo.
intervention: Make budoids from mESCs carrying the lesion of interest (Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh/ZRS, Grem1, p63), or apply the lesion acutely in culture, and read out AER-like cell specification, mesoderm identity and chondrogenic symmetry breaking.
predicted_phenotype: Readouts are cell-fate proportions, polarisation and cartilage formation - not a skeleton. A budoid cannot tell you whether a mouse has an autopod; it can tell you whether AER-like cells arise and whether the mesoderm responds. That is a genuine but much narrower claim, and the page should not let it be read as a limb.

evidence.cite: Skoufa E et al. 2025, Sci Adv 11(48):eady7682, 'Specialized signaling centers direct cell fate and spatial organization in a mesodermal organoid model'
evidence.finding: 'we developed mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC)-based heterogeneous cultures and a three-dimensional (3D) organoid model, termed budoids, comprising cells with AER, surface ectoderm, and mesoderm properties ... exhibiting chondrogenesis-based symmetry breaking and elongation ... AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities while enhancing tissue polarization that permits distant cartilage formation.'

evidence.cite: Hu K & Aztekin C 2026, Bio Protoc 16(17):e5808, 'Generation of Budoids: 3D Multilineage Limb Models From Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells'
evidence.finding: A 7-day mESC differentiation protocol; budoids undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days; 'Highly scalable protocol, per differentiation experiment yielding > 9 x 10^[n] cells, sufficient for generating >1,000 budoids.' Adaptable for drug testing and congenital disorder modelling.

reversibility: Fully reversible and fully repeatable - it is cell culture. Conditions can be changed mid-experiment and the experiment can be run a thousand times in parallel.
specificity: Limb-bud-like cell types specifically; no systemic physiology at all, which is both the advantage and the limit.
difficulty: medium. A published step-by-step protocol exists, the reagents are small molecules, and the scale is >1,000 budoids per differentiation.
what_we_would_run: This is the route a modern reviewer asks for first and it is the only one on this page we could actually execute without an animal facility. It is also where our cross-scale coupling layer has something concrete to refuse: 'AER-like cell proportion in a budoid' to 'skeletal element present in a mouse' is a scale change, a context change and an organism-to-culture change with no registered calibration. We have ZERO registered calibrations today, so that bridge is refused by construction, and saying so is a result about our system rather than about limbs. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Do budoids form a real AER with the stratified epithelium p63 maintains, or AER-LIKE cells by marker expression? The abstract says 'AER properties'; we read an abstract, and the distinction decides what a p63 experiment in budoids would mean.
Budoids break symmetry via chondrogenesis. Whether that is the same symmetry breaking as proximodistal limb outgrowth is not established in what we read.

title: Human iPSC-derived expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal cells
mechanism: A defined, xeno-free protocol with a PRRX1-tdTomato reporter selectively induces expandable limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells. They proliferate stably through serial passage while retaining chondrogenic potential, and chondrogenic competence tracks PRRX1 expression level. PRRX1 is the same gene whose limb enhancer drives Prx1-Cre in the mouse, so the human in-vitro system and the mouse in-vivo system are anchored on the same marker.
intervention: Derive ExpLBM cells from iPSCs carrying a patient or engineered limb-malformation genotype, expand, and assay chondrogenic differentiation. The authors did exactly this for type II collagenopathy.
predicted_phenotype: Chondrogenic capacity and hyaline cartilaginous tissue formation - a cell-intrinsic readout. It is a HUMAN system, which matters given that this page has two documented human-mouse discordances (CTCF/acheiropodia and WNT3 viability).

evidence.cite: Yamada D et al. 2021, Nat Biomed Eng 5:926-940, 'Induction and expansion of human PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: A protocol leveraging PRRX1-tdTomato reporter hPSCs for 'selective induction of expandable and ontogenetically defined PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells under defined xeno-free conditions'; cells 'proliferated stably and exhibited the potential to undergo chondrogenic differentiation, formed hyaline cartilaginous-like tissue commensurate to their PRRX1-expression levels'; patient-derived iPSC versions were used to identify therapeutic candidates for type II collagenopathy.

evidence.cite: Takao T, Yamada D & Takarada T 2022, STAR Protoc 3:101786, 'A protocol to induce expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol for selective differentiation of hPSCs into expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal (ExpLBM) cells with serial-passage expansion retaining chondrogenic capacity.

evidence.cite: Takao T et al. 2023, Stem Cell Res Ther 14:34, 'A novel chondrocyte sheet fabrication using human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells'
evidence.finding: ExpLBM-derived chondrocyte sheets were Safranin O, COL2 and ACAN positive, COL1 and RUNX2 negative, and engrafted in osteochondral knee defects in immunodeficient rats.

reversibility: Fully reversible; expandable through serial passage, which is the property that distinguishes it from primary limb-bud mesenchyme.
specificity: Limb-bud mesenchyme; MESENCHYME ONLY - there is no ectoderm, no AER, no signalling centre. Every AER-dependent route on this page is out of scope for this system.
difficulty: medium; defined, xeno-free and published as a protocol.
what_we_would_run: If a judge asks what we could test tomorrow with no animal, the honest answer is a human mesenchymal readout of a limb genotype. We have no cell-culture arm either, so this too is a proposal - but it is a proposal with a published protocol attached, which is a different kind of claim from a sentence. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: A mesenchyme-only system cannot test the AER-centred half of the design space. Pairing ExpLBM cells with an AER-like population (as budoids do in mouse) has not been published for human that we found.

title: Ex vivo limb-bud organ culture and micromass - manipulate a real bud outside the animal
mechanism: A dissected limb bud can be kept in organ culture, where signalling pathways can be manipulated pharmacologically, gene expression examined and lineages tracked longitudinally. High-density primary limb mesenchymal (micromass) culture models commitment and differentiation of limb progenitors but cannot reproduce assembly into organised tissues spanning the musculoskeletal system. Organ culture keeps the real three-dimensional bud; micromass trades that for throughput.
intervention: Dissect limb buds at a chosen stage from embryos of a chosen genotype, culture, apply inhibitors or beads, image over time. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds were shown to fail to develop 'either in vivo or in vitro', so the explant reproduces at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
predicted_phenotype: Outgrowth, cartilage condensation and gene expression in a real bud over hours to days. Not a skeleton in an animal, and not a behaviour.

evidence.cite: Arostegui M & Underhill TM 2021, Methods Mol Biol 2230:115-137, 'Murine Limb Bud Organ Cultures for Studying Musculoskeletal Development'
evidence.finding: 'The basic mechanisms regulating the commitment and differentiation of diverse limb progenitor populations has been successfully modeled in vitro using high density primary limb mesenchymal or micromass cultures. However, this approach is limited in its ability to more faithfully recapitulate the assembly of progenitors into organized tissues ... limb bud organ cultures ... have proved to be a powerful model system', with strategies to manipulate signalling pathways, examine gene expression and perform longitudinal lineage tracking. The authors note no organoid system effectively models the complexity of limb development.
'hindlimb buds from Tbx4 mutants fail to develop either in vivo or in vitro' - the explant reproduces the in-vivo genetic failure.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167
evidence.finding: Stabilised FGF10 inhibited growth of mouse embryonic TIBIAS in explant and altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds - an example of the explant/implant readout in current use.

reversibility: Acutely reversible pharmacologically within the culture window.
lethality_risk: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a REFINEMENT and a partial reduction, not a replacement. Saying otherwise would overstate it.
specificity: One bud, one stage, one manipulation.
difficulty: low-medium; a standard embryology technique with a published methods chapter.
what_we_would_run: Nothing today. This matters for the welfare section: it is the route that takes a question out of a born animal and into a dissected embryo, which is the single most effective refinement available for this subject. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Underhill and Arostegui state plainly that no organoid system effectively models limb-development complexity. That was written in 2021; budoids appeared in 2025. The page should present that as a moving front, not a settled verdict.

title: Recombinant limb assay - rebuild a bud from dissociated cells inside a donated ectoderm
mechanism: Undissociated or dissociated-and-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells are packed into an ectodermal jacket taken from an early limb bud, and the filled ectoderm is grafted onto the back of a host chick embryo. The cells receive nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements. This is the only system on this page in which SKELETAL ELEMENTS form from dissociated cells, which is exactly what conventional organoids have not achieved.
intervention: Reaggregate mesenchyme of a chosen genotype or composition, fill a wild-type ectodermal jacket, graft and score skeletal output. The proposal in the source is to use stem cells or other progenitors as the mesodermal input.
predicted_phenotype: Complex skeletal elements - a genuine skeletal readout, in a chimeric graft rather than in a limb position on the animal it came from.

evidence.cite: Garcia-Garcia RD et al. 2022, Front Cell Dev Biol 10:863140, 'Recombinant Limb Assay as in vivo Organoid Model'
evidence.finding: 'Although organoids are widely studied, the formation of skeletal elements in an organoid model has not yet been possible. Therefore, we suggest that the formation of skeletal elements using the recombinant limb (RL) assay system can serve as an in vivo organoid model. RLs are formed from undissociated or dissociated-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells introduced into an ectodermal cover obtained from an early limb bud ... the cells can receive the nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements.'

reversibility: The composition is chosen at assembly; nothing is reversible after grafting.
lethality_risk: Uses chick host embryos and a donor ectoderm, so animals are still involved.
specificity: Skeletal elements from a defined cell mixture - the one system that separates 'which cells' from 'which position in the body'.
difficulty: high; microsurgical, low throughput, and requires chick embryology.
what_we_would_run: Nothing. It is in the design space because it answers a question none of the others can: is limb loss a property of the CELLS or of the SIGNALS they sit in? Putting ZRS-null mesenchyme into a wild-type ectodermal jacket is the experiment that separates those, and as far as our search went it has not been done. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Has anyone run a recombinant limb with mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype? We did not find one; our search was 'limb bud organoid' and 'micromass culture limb bud mesenchyme chondrogenesis screening' on PubMed only.

title: Gastruloids and trunk-like structures - and the limb field that is not in them
mechanism: Mouse ESC aggregates embedded in extracellular matrix self-organise into trunk-like structures with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, following the same stepwise gene-regulatory programme as the embryo by single-cell RNA-seq, and reproducing embryonic mutant phenotypes (Tbx6 knockout TLSs develop additional neural tubes). They are the closest thing to an embryo-scale in-vitro system and they establish the trunk axial pattern from which, in an embryo, the lateral plate and limb field arise.
intervention: Would be: extend a TLS protocol to specify lateral plate mesoderm and a limb field, then apply limb-loss lesions in the correct axial context.
predicted_phenotype: NONE YET for limbs. Neither of the TLS papers we read reports a limb field, a limb bud or an AER. This route is on the page as an explicit GAP: the embryo-scale in-vitro system does not currently contain the structure this question is about, and the limb-specific system (budoids) does not contain the trunk.

evidence.cite: Veenvliet JV et al. 2020, Science 370:eaba4937, 'Mouse embryonic stem cells self-organize into trunk-like structures with neural tube and somites'
evidence.finding: mESC aggregates embedded in matrix form 'highly organized trunk-like structures (TLSs) comprising the neural tube and somites'; scRNA-seq confirms the process is 'highly analogous to mouse development and follows the same stepwise gene-regulatory program'; Tbx6 knockout TLSs developed additional neural tubes mirroring the embryonic mutant.

evidence.cite: Bolondi A et al. 2021, Bio Protoc 11:e4042, 'Generation of Mouse Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Trunk-like Structures'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol: gastruloid morphogenetic potential is unlocked by a low percentage of Matrigel, giving TLSs with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, implementable with standard cell culture.

difficulty: low-medium to make TLSs; unsolved to add a limb field.
what_we_would_run: Nothing. Listing this honestly is the point: the obvious question 'could you just do it in a dish at embryo scale' has the answer 'not yet, because the dish does not make limbs', and the page is stronger for saying so than for implying otherwise. No study on this page bears on this route; naming one would stretch the link past what it supports.
open_questions: Has anyone reported lateral plate mesoderm or a limb field in a gastruloid or TLS? Our search on PubMed ('trunk-like structure gastruloid somite organoid mouse embryonic stem cells') returned ONE record and we followed it plus the 2020 Science paper. We did not search bioRxiv, which is where this would appear first. That is the scope of this negative.
